01 / MY JOURNEY

From writing code to leading programs.

I didn't plan to become a program manager. I followed the work — and the work kept getting bigger.

My career started at GlobalLogic, where I wrote SQL and PL/SQL queries for Google Maps — authoring geospatial data pipelines that had to be accurate at scale. I was ranked top performer in quality and speed for six consecutive months. That early discipline of getting things right, not just getting them done, stayed with me.

At TCS I grew into a project lead — building OBIEE reports and BI Publisher dashboards for PepsiCo and other global clients, while learning to manage sprint backlogs and coordinate teams across competing priorities. That is where I discovered that the technical work and the delivery work are inseparable. You cannot lead a program you do not understand, and you cannot build software without someone keeping the whole picture in view.

Oracle is where I grew into a program leader. In my first stint I built REST API integrations, developed Oracle APEX applications, and authored PL/SQL procedures — hands-on technical delivery. In my second stint, as Principal Technical Program Manager, the scope widened to enterprise governance: managing four major releases per year, leading cross-organizational dependency programs across nine external teams, building AI-powered delivery agents, and reporting directly to VP and SVP leadership.

I am a Certified Scrum Master — CSM and SAFe — and PMP certified. Not because the certificates matter, but because the discipline behind them does. I have run hundreds of sprint ceremonies, managed backlogs of 200+ items across concurrent workstreams, and coached teams on why velocity matters and what a good retrospective actually produces.

Outside of work, I am based in Hyderabad with my family. I follow cricket, stay close to how AI tools are changing delivery, and believe that the best program managers are the ones who remember what it felt like to be the developer in the room.

02 / HOW I WORK

The things I come back to.

These are not values on a slide. They are the habits that shaped every program I have led.

01
🔭

See the risk before it becomes a crisis.

I build escalation mechanisms, dependency trackers, and daily visibility systems specifically because the best risk management happens before anyone else notices. Surprises are a process failure, not bad luck.

02
🏗️

Build systems, not workarounds.

Every broken process I touch gets replaced with something that works when I am not in the room. APEX dashboards, reconciliation matrices, governance frameworks — things that scale beyond any single person.

03
🤝

Influence without authority is the real skill.

The hardest programs involve teams that do not report to you. I use data, governance cadences, and clear impact visibility — not pressure — to move teams. And they come back to work with me again.

04
💬

Translate, do not just communicate.

I can sit in an architectural discussion with engineers and understand the real implications. And I can distill that complexity into a single RAG status and three decision points for a VP. Both sides trust me more because of it.

05
🤖

Use AI as a delivery multiplier — honestly.

I have built and deployed AI agents in production delivery workflows. I use AI to accelerate — automated sprint documentation, quality validation, stakeholder reporting. Not to replace judgment. To free it up.

06
🎯

Own the outcome, not just the plan.

A plan is only as good as what it delivers. I stay close to execution — tracking daily, surfacing slippage early, and holding the accountability conversation before it becomes a miss. The plan serves the outcome, never the other way around.
